title: Notations
body_md:
Bold symbols denote vectors (e.g., $ m{x},  m{y} \in \mathbb{R}^n$), and bold functions denote vector-valued maps (e.g., $ m{f} \colon \mathbb{R}^n \mapsto \mathbb{R}^s$, $ m{y}\! =\!  m{f}( m{x})$). The Euclidean norm of $ m{x} \!\in \!\mathbb{R}^n$ is $
orm{ m{x}}_2$. For a radius $r\!>\!0$, the open Euclidean ball centered at $ m a \in \mathbb R^n$ is
$B_r( m a)\!=\!\{ m x\!\in\!\mathbb R^n\!:\!\| m x- m a\|_2\!<\!r\}$ and the closed ball is denoted as $\overline B_r( m a)$, where the overline means the closure of the set. For a point $ m x\in\mathbb R^n$ and a set $S\subset\mathbb R^n$, the distance from $ m x$ to $S$ is $\mathrm{dist}( m x,S)=\inf_{ m y\in S}\| m x- m y\|_2.$ For a symmetric matrix $Q\!\in\!\mathbb R^{n	imes n}$, we write $Q\!\succ\!0$ to denote that $Q$ is positive definite. For a $\mathcal{C}^k$ map $ m f=[f_1,\ldots,f_n]^	op:\mathbb{R}^n\mapsto\mathbb{R}^n$, the $k$-linear operator $
abla^k m f( m a):(\mathbb{R}^n)^k \mapsto \mathbb{R}^n$ denotes the $k$-th partial-derivative tensor with entries $ ig(
abla^k m f( m a) ig)_{\ell,i_1,\ldots,i_k}= rac{\partial^k f_\ell}{\partial x_{i_1}\cdots\partial x_{i_k}}( m a)$, symmetric in $(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$. For $ m v_1,\ldots, m v_k\in\mathbb R^n$,
$
abla^k m f( m a)( m v_1,\ldots, m v_k)$ denotes the corresponding multilinear evaluation. In particular, we use the shorthand $
abla^{k} m f( m a)( m x)^{(k)}=
abla^{k} m f( m a)( m x,\ldots, m x)\in\mathbb R^n$. When $ m f$ is $\mathcal{C}^1$, we write $J m f( m a)=
abla  m f( m a)$ for its Jacobian. For a scalar $V:\mathbb{R}^n\mapsto\mathbb{R}$, $
abla V$ is its gradient and the Lie derivative along $ m f$ is $\mathcal{L}_f V( m x)=
abla V( m x)^	op  m f( m x)$. The induced operator norm is $\|
abla^{k} m f( m a)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\| m x_i\|_2=1}\, ig\|
abla^{k} m f( m a)( m x_1,\ldots, m x_k) ig\|_2.$

label: thm:lf_implies_stability
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:lf_implies_stability}
If a Lyapunov function $V: \Omega \mapsto \mathbb{R}$ exists, then the equilibrium point $\bm{a}$ of $\dot{\bm{x}} = \bm{f}(\bm{x})$ is locally stable. If $V(\bm x)$ is a strict Lyapunov function, then $\bm{a}$ is locally asymptotically stable.

name: Taylor Polynomial of $p$th-order

label: thm:lagrange
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:lagrange}
Let $\mathcal X \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be open, $\bm{f} \colon \mathcal X \mapsto \mathbb{R}^n$ be $\mathcal{C}^{p+1}$ ($p \geq 0$), and assume $\exists m > 0$ such that
$\norm{\nabla^{p+1}\bm{f}(\bm{x})}_{\mathrm{op}} \leq m$ for all $\bm{x} \!\in\! \mathcal X$. Fix $\bm{a} \!\in\! \mathcal X$ and $\bm{h} \!\in\! \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\{\bm{a} + \theta\bm{h} \colon\! 0 \leq \theta\leq 1\} \subset \mathcal X$ (if $\mathcal X$ is convex, $\bm{a} \!\in\! \mathcal X$ and $\bm{a} + \bm{h} \!\in\! \mathcal X$ suffice). Define the remainder
\[
\bm{\rho}_{p+1}(\bm{h}) = \bm{f}(\bm{a} + \bm{h}) - \sum_{k=0}^p \frac{1}{k!}\nabla^{k}\bm{f}(\bm{a})(\bm{h})^{(k)},\quad \text{then}
\]
\[
\norm{\bm{\rho}_{p+1}(\bm{h})}_2 \leq m \frac{\norm{\bm{h}}_2^{p+1}}{(p+1)!}.
\]
head: environment
name: Bound for Vector Field Taylor Remainder

title: Proof
body_md: ee Theorem 5.6.2 of \cite{cartan1971differential} and p.~492 of \cite{lang2005undergraduate}.
head: environment

label: rem:compact_bound
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:compact_bound}
The global bound $m$ in Lemma~\ref{thm:lagrange} may fail on unbounded domains. For local analysis around a fixed point $\bm a\in\mathcal X$, since $\mathcal X$ is open, choose $r>0$ such that $\overline B_r(\bm a)\subset\mathcal X$, and set
$\Omega=B_r(\bm a)$. Then $\overline{\Omega}$ is compact by the Heine--Borel theorem \cite[p.~40]{Rudin1976}. Since
$\bm f\in\mathcal C^{p+1}(\mathcal X;\mathbb R^n)$, the map $\bm x\mapsto \|\nabla^{p+1}\bm f(\bm x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ is continuous on
$\overline{\Omega}$ and attains a finite maximum $m_{\overline{\Omega}}:=\max_{\bm x\in\overline{\Omega}}
\|\nabla^{p+1}\bm f(\bm x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$. Hence, for every $\bm h$ such that the segment
$\{\bm a+\theta\bm h:0\leq\theta\leq1\}$ is contained in $\overline{\Omega}$, the Taylor remainder satisfies
$\|\bm\rho_{p+1}(\bm h)\|_2\leq m_{\overline{\Omega}}\|\bm h\|_2^{p+1}/(p+1)!$.
head: environment
name: Local Taylor Remainder Bound

label: thm:lie-decay-region
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:lie-decay-region}
Let $\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^{n}$ be nonempty and open, and let
$\bm f\in\mathcal C^{p+1}(\mathcal X;\mathbb R^{n})$ for some $p\ge0$.
Fix $\bm a\in\mathcal X$ such that $\bm f(\bm a)=\bm0$, and write the
$p$th-order Taylor expansion of $\bm f$ at $\bm a$ as
$\bm f(\bm x)=\bm f_p(\bm x)+\bm\rho_{p+1}(\bm x)$, where $\bm f_p$ denotes
the $p$th-order Taylor polynomial of $\bm f$ at $\bm a$
(Definition~\ref{def:Taylor_polynomial}, equation~\eqref{eq:taylor_poly}),
and $\bm\rho_{p+1}$ is the remainder (Lemma~\ref{thm:lagrange}). Suppose there exists a bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathcal X$ with $\bm a\in\Omega$ and $\overline{\Omega}\subset\mathcal X$, and a constant $m>0$ such that $\|\nabla^{p+1}\bm f(\bm x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le m$ $\forall\bm x\in\overline{\Omega}$. Define $k_p=m/(p+1)!$. Suppose there exists a
polynomial $V:\Omega\mapsto\mathbb R$, with $V(\bm a)=0$ and
$V(\bm x)>0$ $\forall\bm x\in\Omega\setminus\{\bm a\}$, such that:
\begin{enumerate}\renewcommand{(\roman{enumi})}{(\roman{enumi})}
    \item\label{b1} $\nabla V(\bm x)^{\!\top}\bm f_{p}(\bm x)\le0$ for all $\bm x\in\Omega$;

    \item\label{b2} $\nabla V(\bm x)\neq0$ for all $\bm x\in\Omega\setminus\{\bm a\}$;

    \item\label{dec-2} There exist $\mu>0$, $\delta>0$, and $0\le c\le p+1$ such that, for all
    $\bm x\in(B_\delta(\bm a)\cap\Omega)\setminus\{\bm a\}$,
    \begin{equation}\label{eqdec-2}
    -\nabla V(\bm x)^{\!\top}\bm f_{p}(\bm x)
    \ge
    \mu\,\|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2\,\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2^c,
    \end{equation}
    and, if $c=p+1$, assume additionally that $\mu>k_p$.
\end{enumerate}

Define $\bar r=\min\{(\mu/k_p)^{1/(p+1-c)},\delta,\mathrm{dist}(\bm a,\partial\Omega)\}$ if $c<p+1$, and
$\bar r=\min\{\delta,\mathrm{dist}(\bm a,\partial\Omega)\}$ if $c=p+1$.
Then, for every $r\in(0,\bar r)$, $V$ is a strict local Lyapunov function for
the original system $\dot{\bm x}=\bm f(\bm x)$ on $B_r(\bm a)$. In particular,
$\bm a$ is a locally asymptotically stable equilibrium of
$\dot{\bm x}=\bm f(\bm x)$. Moreover, define
$\gamma_r^\star=\min_{\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2=r}V(\bm x)$,
$S_\gamma=\{\bm x\in\Omega:V(\bm x)\le\gamma\}$, and let
$\mathcal L_\gamma$ be the connected component of $S_\gamma$ containing
$\bm a$. Then $\gamma_r^\star>0$, and every
$\gamma\in(0,\gamma_r^\star)$ satisfies
$\mathcal L_\gamma\subset B_r(\bm a)$, $\mathcal L_\gamma$ is positively
invariant, and $\mathcal L_\gamma\subset\mathrm{ROA}(\bm a)$.
head: environment
name: Sufficient Conditions for Stability Transfer

title: Proof
body_md:
ix any $r\in(0,\bar r)$. Regardless of whether $c<p+1$ or $c=p+1$,
$\bar r$ is defined so that $\bar r\le\delta$ and
$\bar r\le\mathrm{dist}(\bm a,\partial\Omega)$. Hence
$B_r(\bm a)\subset B_\delta(\bm a)\cap\Omega$. Moreover, for every
$\bm x\in B_r(\bm a)$, the segment
$\{\bm a+\theta(\bm x-\bm a):0\le\theta\le1\}$ lies in
$B_r(\bm a)$, and hence in $\Omega\subset\mathcal X$. Therefore, by
Lemma~\ref{thm:lagrange} with the assumed bound $m$ on $\overline{\Omega}$,
$\|\bm\rho_{p+1}(\bm x)\|_2\le
k_p\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2^{p+1}$ $\forall\bm x\in B_r(\bm a)$.

\textit{Case 1:} \(c<p+1\). Let
$r_1=(\mu/k_p)^{1/(p+1-c)}$. By the definition of $\bar r$, we have
$r<r_1$. For every \(\bm x\in B_r(\bm a)\setminus\{\bm a\}\), we have
$\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2<r<r_1$. This implies
$\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2^{p+1-c}<r_1^{p+1-c}=\mu/k_p$, and thus
$k_p\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2^{p+1-c}<\mu$. Since
$\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2^c>0$ for $\bm x\neq\bm a$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ineq}
k_p\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2^{p+1}<\mu\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2^c.
\end{equation}
By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, the local remainder estimate above, and
assumption~\ref{dec-2},
\begin{align*}
&\nabla V(\bm x)^{\!\top} \bm f(\bm x)
  \le \nabla V(\bm x)^{\!\top} \bm f_{p}(\bm x)
      + \big| \nabla V(\bm x)^{\!\top} \bm{\rho}_{p+1}(\bm x)\big| \\
  &\le \nabla V(\bm x)^{\!\top} \bm f_{p}(\bm x)
      + \|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2  \|\bm{\rho}_{p+1}(\bm x)\|_2  \\
  &\le \nabla V(\bm x)^{\!\top} \bm f_{p}(\bm x)
      + \|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2  k_{p} \|\bm x - \bm a\|_2^{p+1} \\
  &\le  -\mu\,\|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2\,\|\bm x-\bm a\|^c_2
       + k_{p}\,\|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2\,\|\bm x-\bm a\|^{p+1}_2  \\
  &=\|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2 (-\mu\|\bm x-\bm a\|^c_2 +k_{p}\|\bm x-\bm a\|^{p+1}_2).
\end{align*}
Using \eqref{eq:ineq}, the term
$-\mu\|\bm x-\bm a\|^c_2+k_{p}\|\bm x-\bm a\|^{p+1}_2<0$.
By assumption~\ref{b2}, $\|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2>0$ for
$\bm x\neq\bm a$. Therefore, $\nabla V(\bm x)^{\!\top}\bm f(\bm x)<0$ for all
$\bm x\in B_r(\bm a)\setminus\{\bm a\}$.

\textit{Case 2:} \(c=p+1\). For any
$\bm x\in B_r(\bm a)\setminus\{\bm a\}$, using the local remainder estimate
above and assumption~\ref{dec-2},
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{L}_f V(\bm x)
&\le
\|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2
(-\mu\|\bm x-\bm a\|^{p+1}_2
+k_{p}\|\bm x-\bm a\|^{p+1}_2)\\
&=
\|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2\|\bm x-\bm a\|^{p+1}_2(k_p-\mu).
\end{align*}
Since $\mu>k_p$, the term $(k_p-\mu)$ is strictly negative. By
assumption~\ref{b2} and $\bm x\neq\bm a$,
$\|\nabla V(\bm x)\|_2\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2^{p+1}>0$. Thus,
$\nabla V(\bm x)^{\!\top}\bm f(\bm x)<0$ on
$B_r(\bm a)\setminus\{\bm a\}$.

In both cases, and noting that $\mathcal L_fV(\bm a)=0$, we have constructed a
radius $r>0$ such that $V(\bm x)$ is positive definite on $B_r(\bm a)$ and
$\mathcal L_fV(\bm x)$ is negative definite on
$B_r(\bm a)\setminus\{\bm a\}$. This satisfies the conditions for $V$ to be a
strict local Lyapunov function (Definition~\ref{def:local_LF}). By
Lemma~\ref{thm:lf_implies_stability}, the existence of a strict local Lyapunov
function implies that the equilibrium $\bm a$ is locally asymptotically stable
for $\dot{\bm x}=\bm f(\bm x)$.

Now consider $\gamma_r^\star=\min_{\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2=r}V(\bm x)$. Since
$r<\mathrm{dist}(\bm a,\partial\Omega)$, the sphere
$\{\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2=r\}$ is compact and contained in $\Omega$. Since $V$ is
continuous and positive definite, $\gamma_r^\star>0$. Fix
$\gamma\in(0,\gamma_r^\star)$, and let
$S_\gamma=\{\bm x\in\Omega:V(\bm x)\le\gamma\}$ and
$\mathcal L_\gamma$ be the connected component of $S_\gamma$ containing
$\bm a$. We claim that $\mathcal L_\gamma\subset B_r(\bm a)$. If not, then
since $\mathcal L_\gamma$ is connected and contains $\bm a$, it must intersect
the sphere $\{\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2=r\}$. But on that sphere,
$V(\bm x)\ge\gamma_r^\star>\gamma$, contradicting
$\mathcal L_\gamma\subset S_\gamma$.

Next, $\mathcal L_\gamma$ is positively invariant. Let $\bm x(t)$ be a
trajectory with $\bm x(0)\in\mathcal L_\gamma$. While
$\bm x(t)\in B_r(\bm a)$, one has $\mathcal L_fV(\bm x(t))\le0$, hence
$V(\bm x(t))\le V(\bm x(0))\le\gamma$. Therefore the trajectory cannot cross
the sphere $\{\|\bm x-\bm a\|_2=r\}$, because there
$V\ge\gamma_r^\star>\gamma$. Thus $\bm x(t)\in B_r(\bm a)$ for all
$t\ge0$, and hence $\bm x(t)\in S_\gamma$ for all $t\ge0$. Since
$t\mapsto\bm x(t)$ is continuous, the image $\bm x([0,\infty))$ is a connected
subset of $S_\gamma$ containing $\bm x(0)\in\mathcal L_\gamma$. By definition
of $\mathcal L_\gamma$ as the connected component of $S_\gamma$ containing
$\bm a$, it follows that $\bm x([0,\infty))\subset\mathcal L_\gamma$.

Now $S_\gamma\cap\overline B_r(\bm a)$ is closed in the compact
$\overline B_r(\bm a)$, hence compact. Since $\mathcal L_\gamma$ is a
connected component of $S_\gamma\cap\overline B_r(\bm a)$, it is closed in
$S_\gamma\cap\overline B_r(\bm a)$ and then compact. Since
$\mathcal L_\gamma$ is compact and positively invariant, and
$\mathcal L_fV(\bm x)<0$ $\forall\bm x\in\mathcal L_\gamma\setminus\{\bm a\}$, the set
$\{\bm x\in\mathcal L_\gamma:\mathcal L_fV(\bm x)=0\}$ is $\{\bm a\}$. Hence,
by LaSalle's principle~\cite[Thm.~4.4]{khalil2002nonlinear}, every trajectory
starting in $\mathcal L_\gamma$ converges to $\bm a$. Therefore,
$\mathcal L_\gamma\subset\mathrm{ROA}(\bm a)$.
head: environment

label: prop:gamma-lower-bound
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:gamma-lower-bound}
Let $V$ satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:lie-decay-region}, and let
$\gamma_r^\star$ and $\mathcal L_\gamma$ be defined as in that theorem. Write
the translated polynomial $V(\bm a+\bm z)$ as the finite sum of its homogeneous
components,
$V(\bm a+\bm z)=\sum_{d=d_0}^{D}V_d(\bm z)$, where each $V_d$ is homogeneous of
degree $d$, and $d_0\ge2$ is the first index such that $V_{d_0}\neq0$. This
decomposition is available for any polynomial $V$ and does not require $V$
itself to be homogeneous. If, in addition, $V_{d_0}$ is positive definite,
then, with
$m_{d_0}=\min_{\|\bm z\|_2=1}V_{d_0}(\bm z)$ and
$b_d=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}|c_{d,\alpha}|$ when
$V_d(\bm z)=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}c_{d,\alpha}\bm z^\alpha$, one has
$\gamma_r^\star\ge\underline\gamma(r)=m_{d_0}r^{d_0}-\sum_{d=d_0+1}^{D}b_dr^d$.
Consequently, if $\underline\gamma(r)>0$, then every
$\gamma\in(0,\underline\gamma(r))$ satisfies
$\mathcal L_\gamma\subset\mathrm{ROA}(\bm a)$.
head: environment
name: Explicit Lower Bound for $\gamma_r^\star$

title: Proof
body_md:
ince $V_{d_0}$ is homogeneous and positive definite,
$V_{d_0}(\bm z)\ge m_{d_0}\|\bm z\|_2^{d_0}$. For each $d>d_0$, write
$V_d(\bm z)=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}c_{d,\alpha}\bm z^\alpha$ and
$b_d=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}|c_{d,\alpha}|$, so that
$|V_d(\bm z)|\le b_d\|\bm z\|_2^d$. Therefore,
$V(\bm a+\bm z)\ge m_{d_0}\|\bm z\|_2^{d_0}
-\sum_{d=d_0+1}^{D}b_d\|\bm z\|_2^d$. Evaluating on
$\|\bm z\|_2=r$ yields
\[
\gamma_r^\star
=
\min_{\|\bm z\|_2=r}V(\bm a+\bm z)
\ge
m_{d_0}r^{d_0}
-
\sum_{d=d_0+1}^{D}b_dr^d
=
\underline\gamma(r).
\]
Hence, if $\underline\gamma(r)>0$, then every
$\gamma\in(0,\underline\gamma(r))$ satisfies $\gamma<\gamma_r^\star$, and
therefore $\mathcal L_\gamma\subset\mathrm{ROA}(\bm a)$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:lie-decay-region}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Note that the radius $\bar r$ is not maximal. Also, if $V(\bm x)=(\bm x-\bm a)^\top P(\bm x-\bm a),$ with $P=P^\top\succ0$, then $d_0=2$, $m_2=\lambda_{\min}(P)$, and $b_d=0$ for all $d\ge3$. Therefore, the explicit lower bound becomes $\gamma_r^\star  =\underline \gamma (r)=\lambda_{\min}(P)\,r^2.$ Finally, note that the ball $B_{r}(\bm a)$ may or may not be inside $\mathrm{ROA}(\bm a)$, but $\mathcal L_\gamma\subset B_{r}(\bm a)$ and $\mathcal L_\gamma\subset \mathrm{ROA}(\bm a).$
head: environment

label: exmp:first_exmp
title: Example
body_md:
\label{exmp:first_exmp} Consider a pendulum with nonlinear damping $\tanh(\dot\theta)$, with $x_1=\theta$, $x_2=\dot\theta$, $\bm f(\bm x) = [x_2,\; -\sin(x_1) - \tanh(x_2)]^\top.$
The origin is locally asymptotically stable; saddle equilibria at $(\pm\pi,0)$ bound the $\mathrm{ROA}(\bm 0)$. With $p=3$, using $\sin(x_1)=x_1-\tfrac{1}{6}x_1^3+O(x_1^5)$ and $\tanh(x_2)=x_2-\tfrac{1}{3}x_2^3+O(x_2^5)$:
\[
\bm f_3(\bm x) = \begin{bmatrix} x_2 \\ -x_1 - x_2 + \frac{1}{6}x_1^3 + \frac{1}{3}x_2^3 \end{bmatrix},\quad
\bm \rho_4 = \bm f - \bm f_3.
\]
We take the Lyapunov candidate $V(\bm x)=\tfrac12\bm x^\top P\bm x$, where $P=P^\top\succ0$ solves $A^\top P+PA=-I$ for $A=J\bm f(\bm 0)$, 
\[
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\-1 & -1\end{bmatrix} ,\quad
P=\begin{bmatrix}1.500 & 0.500\\ 0.500 & 1.000\end{bmatrix},
\]
where $\lambda_{\min}(P)=0.691,\quad\lambda_{\max}(P)=1.809$. The Lie derivative along $\bm f_3$ is $\mathcal L_{f_3}V(\bm x)=-\tfrac12\|\bm x\|_2^2+\tfrac{1}{12}x_1^4+\tfrac{1}{6}x_1x_2^3+\tfrac{1}{6}x_1^3x_2+\tfrac{1}{3}x_2^4.$ On $\Omega=B_{0.5}(\bm 0)$, the quartic terms satisfy $\left|\tfrac{1}{12}x_1^4 + \tfrac{1}{6}x_1x_2^3 + \tfrac{1}{6}x_1^3x_2 + \tfrac{1}{3}x_2^4\right|
\le \tfrac34 \norm{\bm x}_2^4
\le \tfrac{3}{16}\norm{\bm x}_2^2$, so $\mathcal L_{f_3}V(\bm x)\le-\tfrac{5}{16}\|\bm x\|_2^2\le0$, verifying~\ref{b1}. Condition~\ref{b2} holds since $\nabla V=P\bm x\neq\bm 0$ for $\bm x\neq\bm 0$. For~\ref{dec-2}, choose $c=1$, $\delta=0.5$; since $-\mathcal L_{f_3}V\ge\tfrac{5}{16}\|\bm x\|_2^2$ and $\|\nabla V\|_2\le 1.809\|\bm x\|_2$, condition~\ref{dec-2} holds with $\mu=0.17\le(5/16)/1.809$. To bound the remainder on $\overline{B}_{0.5}(\bm 0)$, we use $\|\nabla^4\bm f(\bm x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|\nabla^4\bm f(\bm x)\|_{\mathrm{F}}$, where the only nonzero fourth-order entries are $\partial^4 f_2/\partial x_1^4=-\sin(x_1)$ and $\partial^4 f_2/\partial x_2^4=-\tanh^{(4)}(x_2)$, 
\[
\|\nabla^4\bm f(\bm x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|\nabla^4\bm f(\bm x)\|_{\mathrm{F}}=\sqrt{\!\left(\tfrac{\partial^4 f_2}{\partial x_1^4}\right)^{\!2}\!+\!\left(\tfrac{\partial^4 f_2}{\partial x_2^4}\right)^{\!2}}.
\]
Numerical evaluation of $\max\|\nabla^4\bm f(\bm x)\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ on $\overline{B}_{0.5}(\bm 0)$ yields $m\le 4.1$, hence $k_p\le0.17$ and $r_1\ge1$. Therefore $\bar r=\min\{r_1,\delta,\mathrm{dist}(\bm 0,\partial\Omega)\}=0.5$, and $V$ is a strict Lyapunov function for $\dot{\bm x}=\bm f(\bm x)$ on every $B_r(\bm 0)$, $r\in(0,0.5)$. Since $V$ is quadratic, $\gamma_r^\star=\underline\gamma(r)=\tfrac12\lambda_{\min}(P)r^2=0.3455\,r^2$. With $r=0.49$, $\gamma_r^\star=0.083$, so every $\gamma\in(0,0.083)$ yields an invariant $\mathcal L_\gamma\subset\mathrm{ROA}(\bm 0)$, see Fig.~\ref{fig:phasePort}.

name: Pendulum with Nonlinear Damping

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\bm x\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $p(\bm x)\in\mathbb R[\bm x]$ be a
multivariate polynomial. We say that $p(\bm x)$ is a sum-of-squares (SOS) polynomial, denoted $p(\bm x)\in\Sigma[\bm x]$, if there exist polynomials $q_1(\bm x),\ldots,q_j(\bm x)\in\mathbb R[\bm x]$ such that
$ p(\bm x)=\sum_{i=1}^{j} q_i(\bm x)^2 .$
head: environment
name: Sum-of-squares (SOS) polynomial

label: exmp:sos_grid_quartic
title: Example
body_md:
\label{exmp:sos_grid_quartic}
We apply Algorithm~\ref{alg:sos_grid_sublevel} to the pendulum of Example~\ref{exmp:first_exmp}, using its $p=5$ polynomial truncation $\bm f_p(\bm x)$ and searching for a quadratic Lyapunov function $V(\bm x)$. We set $\epsilon=1$, $\epsilon_V=\epsilon_{P2}=10^{-6}$, $s=1$, and $c=1$. The SOS-constrained SDP \eqref{eq:sos_feasibility_quartic_generic}, with $\deg(V)=2$, $\deg(p)=2$, and $\deg(q)=4$, is solved on a grid $\delta_k\in[0.5,3]$ of $30$ points using MOSEK~\cite{mosek} via YALMIP~\cite{Lofberg2009}, where each point of the grid took $0.15$ s to run in a 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700H at 2.30GHz. Following Algorithm~\ref{alg:sos_grid_sublevel}, the best certified value is obtained at $\delta^*=1.276$, $L_{\delta^*}=4.775,$ $m_{\delta^*}=52.789.$ Thus $\mu=1/L_{\delta^*}=0.209$, $k_p=m_{\delta^*}/6!=0.0733$, and $ r_1=1.23,$ $\bar r_{\mathrm{best}}=\min\{r_1,\delta^*\}=1.23.$

Therefore, $V^*(\bm x)$ is a strict Lyapunov function of $\dot{\bm x}=\bm f(\bm x)$ on every ball $B_r(\bm0)$ with
$r\in(0,\bar r_{\mathrm{best}})$. For visualization, we choose $r=0.99\bar r_{\mathrm{best}}=1.2212$, which gives
$\gamma_r^\star=1.4954$; hence we take $\gamma=1.1963<\gamma_r^\star$.
Fig.~\ref{fig:phasePort_sos} shows the phase portrait and compares the certified balls for $p=1$, $p=3$, and $p=5$, with $\bar r=0.697$, $1.020$, and $1.23$, respectively. For the reported $p=5$ certificate, the displayed connected sublevel set
$\mathcal L_\gamma=\{\bm x\in\Omega:V^*(\bm x)\le\gamma\}\subset B_r(\bm0)$
is positively invariant and satisfies
$\mathcal L_\gamma\subset\mathrm{ROA}(\bm0)$.
head: environment
name: Maximal Threshold Radius by Grid Search

label: exmp:min_effort_lqr
title: Example
body_md:
\label{exmp:min_effort_lqr}
Consider the nonpolynomial control system $\dot{\bm x} = [ x_2,\; x_1 + x_1^3 - 0.1 \tanh(x_2) + u ]^\top.$
The origin is an unstable equilibrium for $u=0$. We aim to find the LQR controller $\bm u = -K_R \bm x $, obtained by solving the algebraic Riccati equation with $Q=I$, that uses the largest scalar $R$ while ensuring $\bm x_0 = [-0.57, 0.57]^\top\!\in\mathrm{ROA}(\bm 0)$.
We use the $p=5$ Taylor approximation $\bm f_{cl,p}(\bm x)$ of the closed loop system $\dot{\bm x} = \bm f(\bm x, -K_R \bm x)$. We search for a quartic Lyapunov function $V(\bm x)$ using the relaxation \eqref{eq:sos_decay_cond} with $\epsilon=1.0$, $s=1$.

Following Algorithm~\ref{alg:min_effort_lqr_sublevel}, searching over $R \in [1, 100]$ (logarithmically spaced, 25 points, from largest to smallest), we find $R^* = 21.544$ that certifies the initial condition $\bm x_0$, where each point took around $0.18$ s to run in a 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700H at 2.30 GHz. The corresponding gain is $K_{R^*} = [2.0229, 1.9254]$. For this controller, the SOS problem finds a valid quartic $V(\bm x)$ and $\delta = 0.9673$ such that $V(\bm x_0)=29.132<\gamma<\hat\gamma_r$, with $\gamma=29.139$, then the initial condition $\bm x_0$ is certified to be within the $\mathrm{ROA}(\bm 0)$.

Figure~\ref{fig:phase_portraits_comparison} shows the system stabilized by the grid-optimized controller $K_{R^*}$. The plot confirms the target initial condition $\bm x_0$ belongs to $\mathcal L_\gamma\subset \mathrm{ROA}(\bm 0)$. This result yields two main benefits: a 16.53\% reduction in control gain norm (vs. $R=1$), and critically, a formal certificate that $\bm x_0$ is within the $\mathrm{ROA}(\bm 0)$ for the nonpolynomial closed loop system, a guarantee that standard LQR design cannot provide alone.
